speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; can you tell me exactly how long you have had these symptoms and if they affect one side of your body more than the other?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The worsening of your symptoms with activity and relief with rest, combined with double vision specifically when looking up or down, strongly suggests a neuromuscular issue. REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Phosphokinase (CPK). REQUEST TEST: Repetitive Nerve Stimulation. Do you have a family history of any muscle or neurological disorders?

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The clinical picture of fatigable weakness (worse with activity, better with rest), diplopia on gaze, and proximal limb weakness is classic for this condition. The normal CPK and nerve studies help rule out primary myopathies or neuropathies. Given the high probability, I will confirm with specific antibodies and imaging.
